body:
Addressed in becb1c28 (docstring follow-up in 17a38764). `execute`'s session block now has a `SQLAlchemyError` arm between the `KeyError` and `Exception` arms: it logs, releases the session through a new `_releaseFailedSession` (a `KeyError` or any other cleanup failure is logged and cannot replace the original error), and raises `RuntimeError('SQL execution failed: ' + _format_db_error(e)) from None` — the same contract as the sessionless path. `tx_registry` is untouched, as you suggested. The max-rows overflow is a plain `RuntimeError`, not a `SQLAlchemyError`, so it still takes the existing arm with its wording and rollback.

Tests (`tests/database/test_execute_session.py`): `test_session_execute_surfaces_the_driver_error` (your twin, plus `[SQL:`, `[parameters:` and `sqlalche.me` asserted absent), `test_session_execute_error_does_not_echo_bound_parameters`, `test_session_execute_failure_releases_the_session`, `test_session_execute_cleanup_failure_does_not_mask_the_driver_error`, `test_session_execute_returns_rows_on_success`, and `test_both_execute_paths_report_a_driver_failure_identically[postgres|mysql]`, which drives one constructed `DBAPIError` through both halves and asserts the two messages are equal and tail-free; the sessionless test gained the same tail assertions. The new tests were run against 28c461e3 first: the session one failed with the raw `OperationalError` carrying `[SQL: SELECT * FROM no_such_table]`.

Verified: 179 passed in `tests/database` + `tests/ai/common/database` with the built engine; whole `packages/ai/tests` 2988 passed / 122 environmental skips; CI __RUN__.
